newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council authorizes force for Albania.
newsitem.headline: UN Council authorizes force for Albania.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council late on Friday authorized an Italian-led force to guard deliveries of food and other necessities in Albania for three months and help the country recover from violence and near-anarchy.

The vote was 14 to 0 with China abstaining on a resolution that invoked Chapter 7 of the U.N. Charter which permits the use of force to protect freedom of movement for the troops in what the council called a "multinational protection force."
China said it could not support the operation because the chaos in Albania was an internal affair and because it did not approve of the use of force.
The mandate for the operation runs for three months at which time the council can decide whether it should be extended. It will be financed by those nations taking part, the resolution said.

The council also welcomed an offer by Italy, contained in separate letter, to take the lead in organizing and commanding the mission whose purpose is to "facilitate the safe and prompt delivery of humanitarian assistance and to help create a secure environment for the missions of international organizations in Albania."

Albania was swept by violence in January when a string of popular savings schemes collapsed, erasing millions of dollars. Rebels seized the south in March in an armed insurrection, blaming President Sali Berisha for the fiasco and demanding that he quit.
